panels.description: Chart 9-style: S&P 500 in real stuff, not dollars. The Commodities Index is the IMF Primary Commodity Price System all-commodities basket (PALLFNF, 2016 = 100): trade-weighted world spot prices for energy (crude, natural gas, coal; crude is about 29%), industrial and precious metals (copper, aluminum, iron ore, gold, etc.), fertilizers, and agriculture. In the book’s words, the stuff you buy, or the stuff that goes into the stuff you buy. Monthly from 2003; can lag the latest S&P print by a month or two. Use a multi-year range; Last 1 hour has no daily bars.

panels.description: Chart 10-style: S&P 500 in food and fiber. The Agricultural Price Index is the IMF PCPS agriculture basket (PAGRI, 2016 = 100): food and beverages (grains, vegetable oils, meat, sugar, coffee, tea, cocoa, fruit) plus agricultural raw materials (cotton, wool, rubber, hides, timber). In the book’s words, the stuff you eat and wear — not energy or industrial metals. Monthly from 1992. Use a multi-year range; Last 1 hour has no daily bars.

panels.description: Chart 12-style: S&P 500 in industrial metals, not dollars. The index is the IMF PCPS base-metals basket (PMETA, 2016 = 100): copper, aluminum, iron ore, nickel, zinc, lead, tin, molybdenum, and uranium — the steel, zinc, copper, and lead the book uses as the automakers’ cost basket. Not gold or silver (those are Chart 13). Monthly from 1992; can lag the S&P by a month or two. Use a multi-year range; Last 1 hour has no daily bars.
